facts.text: Sausal's name comes from Spanish "sauzal", meaning a willow thicket, echoing the riverine groves that line the Rio Grande.
The town sits in a sheltered valley between the Sandia and Manzano Mountains, with the Rio Grande to the east shaping its compact layout.
Sausal enjoys a semi‑arid climate, with hot summers peaking near 92°F and cold winters dropping to about 19°F, plus modest yearly snowfall of six inches.
Founded in the early 19th century as a small farming settlement, Sausal grew alongside Spanish colonial expansion south of Belen and the fertile Rio Grande floodplains.
After World War II, suburban growth from Albuquerque spurred housing development along I‑25, with 2024 median home prices around $314,000 for single‑family lots.
About 30 miles south of Albuquerque, Sausal offers rural charm while staying within reach of the city’s amenities.
